about: The evangelium of the formulary “Sexagesima Sunday” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, when a very great crowd was gathering and people were hurrying from the cities to Jesus, He spoke in a parable: The sower went out to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell by the wayside and was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it. And some fell on a rock and, having sprouted, withered away because it had no moisture. And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up with it and choked it. And some fell on good soil and, having sprouted, yielded fruit a hundredfold. As He said these things, He cried out: Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear. But His disciples asked Him what this parable meant. He said to them: To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to the rest in parables, so that seeing they may not see and hearing may not understand. Now this is the parable: The seed is the word of God. The seed by the wayside represents those who hear. Then the devil comes and takes the word out of their heart, so that they may not be saved through believing. For the seed on the rock represents those who, when they hear, receive the word with joy. These have no roots. They believe for a while and fall away in time of temptation. But the seed that fell among thorns represents those who have heard and, as they go on their way, are choked by the cares, riches and pleasures of life and yield no fruit. But the seed in good soil represents those who hear the word with a good and excellent heart and retain it, and bring forth fruit in patience.

a.g: a very great crowd was gathering
people were hurrying from the cities
the thorns grew up with it and choked it
As He said these things, He cried out
To you it has been given to know
but to the rest in parables
Now the seed by the wayside
so that they may not be saved through believing
For the seed on the rock represents those who
when they hear, receive the word with joy
But the seed that fell among thorns
as they go on their way, are choked by the cares, riches and pleasures of life
with a good and excellent heart
hear the word and retain it

ex.w146: Audíerint can be future perfect indicative or perfect subjunctive. With suscípiunt, it describes hearing before receiving the word. The choice of mood remains uncertain.
